assets.prompt: Repaint the first reference image, a gothic map of the valley of Barovia, so it is no longer drawn on paper, parchment or vellum: the land itself fills the picture, painted as terrain seen from above, like a dark fantasy game's world map. Keep the composition exactly the same: every mountain, the lake, the river, the waterfall and its pool, the forests, the walled town, the hill towns, the ruined mansion, the windmill, the Vistani wagons, the gallows, the village with its church and graveyard, the two knight statues, the castle on its pillar of rock above the chasm and the compass rose stay in the same place, at the same size and with the same outlines. Replace the sheet with real ground: dark heath and moorland in desaturated olive and grey-green, patches of dead brown grass, black earth and mud, a few bare dead trees and scattered rocks, all under a dusky overcast light, darker toward the edges. The swirling pale grey-green fog of the second reference image (the game's title art) rolls in from every edge and hides the land beyond the valley. Keep the colours and mood of the title art: night blues, deep shadows, blood-red glow around Castle Ravenloft with red-lit windows and bats, cold slate mountains with moonlit edges, an ink-dark lake and river with a pale gleam. The compass rose is tarnished iron and gold with a crimson centre, set on the ground. Gothic and foreboding but clearly readable: bold clean black ink outlines and flat cel colour with two or three tones, crisp and sharp, with no grain, noise, speckle or blur. No paper, parchment, vellum, stains, sheet edges, border or frame anywhere. No roads, paths or dotted lines, and no text, letters, labels, numbers, legend or cartouche.
assets.notes: The travel map's art, 3:2 at 2K (--size 2K, 2528x1696) so it stays sharp when the map zooms in; imported lossless with mipmaps. History (all 2026-10-06): barovia_map_a from the layout sketch art/generated/map/barovia_layout.png came out as a bright storybook parchment; the owner asked for the game's gothic tone, so barovia_map_gothic_b repainted it on dark vellum with the title art as the colour reference; the owner then said it needn't look like parchment, so this take repaints the ground as the land itself (dark moorland, grey-green fog from the edges, no paper), the gothic map as the layout reference.
